findings.body:
`GET /api/v2/admin/users` is registered as a bare `http.HandlerFunc` — the previous `middleware.RequireRole("admin")` wrapper is gone. Any unauthenticated or non-admin caller who can hit the server can list users.

Restore the guard on this handler, or apply it once on the subrouter:

```suggestion
	v2 := r.PathPrefix("/api/v2").Subrouter()
	v2.Use(middleware.RequireRole("admin"))
	v2.Handle("/admin/users", http.HandlerFunc(a.listUsers)).Methods("GET")
```

`POST /api/v2/admin/roles` is likewise registered without `middleware.RequireRole("admin")`. This is a privilege-escalation / unauthorized-write path: any client that can reach the endpoint can change roles.

Re-apply the admin role middleware on this handle (or via `v2.Use(...)` on the `/api/v2` subrouter) before merge.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change strips admin authorization from privileged endpoints while relocating them under `/api/v2`.

## What went wrong

The prior routes wrapped both handlers with `middleware.RequireRole("admin")`. The new subrouter registers bare `http.HandlerFunc` values on `GET /api/v2/admin/users` and `POST /api/v2/admin/roles`, so any caller who can reach the server can list users and edit roles.

Moving the admin group under a versioned prefix is fine as an API-layout change, but the role check must stay on every admin handler (or be applied once via `v2.Use(middleware.RequireRole("admin"))` on the subrouter).

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: Base wrapped listUsers with middleware.RequireRole("admin"); head registers a bare HandlerFunc on /api/v2/admin/users with no subrouter Use or other authz, so the admin guard was dropped.

Base registered POST /admin/roles behind middleware.RequireRole("admin"); head moved it to /api/v2/admin/roles as a bare HandlerFunc with no authz middleware or v2.Use guard, so the privilege check was removed.
